e-12372.knowledge_point: Representing a Triple Integral as a Mixed or Repeated Integral
e-12372.problem:
Find the missing limits in the repeated integral

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V
= 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \: \mathrm{d}y,
$$

where $R$ is the type I region defined as

$$
R=\left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: y^2 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \: -1 \leq z \leq x^2+y^2+1\right\}.
$$
e-12372.worked_solution:
A type I region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z)  \: : \: (x,y) \in D, \: u_1(x,y) \leq z \leq u_2(x,y) \big\}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type I region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/1bd4b6d0b1aa955921c1f7855d3fbd95417072a67504d9de9be44dfbbed592e5.png)

 

If $R$ is a type I region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
\iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm d V = \iint\limits_{D} \left[\int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm d z\right]\,\textrm d A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
u_1(x,y) = -1, \qquad u_2(x,y)  = x^2+y^2+1.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V 
= 
\iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{-1}^{x^2+y^2+1} f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}z \right] \mathrm{d}A.
$$

Now, the region $D$ is given by the type II plane region

$$
D =\left\{ (x,y) \: : \: y^2 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1 \right\}.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-1}^{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{2}}^{1}[{\int }_{-1}^{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dx\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{2}}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dx\,dy.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
A type I region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(x,y)\le z\le {u}_{2}(x,y)}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type I region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/1bd4b6d0b1aa955921c1f7855d3fbd95417072a67504d9de9be44dfbbed592e5.png)

 

If $R$ is a type I region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(x,y)=2-x-y\,{u}_{2}(x,y)=4.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{2-x-y}^{4}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA.
$$

A type I region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(x,y)\le z\le {u}_{2}(x,y)}.

$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(x,y)=0,\,{u}_{2}(x,y)=1+xy.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1+xy}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA.
$$

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le {y}^{2},\,-2\le y\le 4}.

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA & ={\int }_{-2}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{1+xy}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dx\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{1+xy}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dx\,dy.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=-2+4=2.
$$

after.worked_solution:
A type I region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(x,y)\le z\le {u}_{2}(x,y)}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type I region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/1bd4b6d0b1aa955921c1f7855d3fbd95417072a67504d9de9be44dfbbed592e5.png)

 

If $R$ is a type I region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(x,y)=-1\,{u}_{2}(x,y)=\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-1}^{\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA.
$$
